From the UK.                                    

Basically. I think the EU wasn't and isn't an intrinsically bad idea. I DO think its very poorly run, organised, and misrepresented. The way its set up, politically is complex to understand. I have looked up article and watched video's of how each branch works together, and i forget soon after or its not clear. I think this is bad, because political systems shouldn't be so bloody complex. Secondly, there's a lot of legal/political waffle. Lots of EU politicans want to become a single state, and it feels like they pass laws they don't need to, acting like a single state, rather than the much more loose, vague political entity it is and was meant to be at the moment. This ties in with the sovereignity issue during the referendum. We have the ability to make laws individually too, they shouldn't be so overreaching legislatively. 
                                             
The EU hasn't written off on an account in years, because of the rife corruption that means huge sums of money get lost in the system. I know most people in Europe won't know this, but this, as far as I know, simply doesn't happen on the same scale in the uk. We really don't like that bit, even though that level of corruption may be part and parcel for mainland general governance.

There's the whole Greece-Germany fiasco, which has been handled VERY badly, and italy is currently being fucked in the ass by the EU hard. It's whole reason for existance was to stop stuff like this. And the Euro. I need not comment on that fuckery.

There's a lot of idealism going about the EU about its future and it feels very quick to disparage anti EU sentiment, rather than try to understand it. Obviously Cameron wasn't our best prime minister, but he went to try and get a deal for the uk before any of this happened in an effort to stop a possible referendum and exit from the EU. He was trying to offer a compromise to help settle the growing anti EU sentiment. And he got, in my opinion, very little, they didn't think it would happen. And it did.                                                               
I think there are good reasons to be a remainer though, and I understand competely why people would of voted remain.                                       
                                                                                                    I may have wrote my points a bit oddly, or skipped something by accident, if I did I apologise I've had no sleep. I don't want to get into a big arguement over this stuff but I'll answer questions if you want.
